summary: One shared literal-pathspec spelling in src/, adopted by commitPaths, job.ts's five call sites and harness/windows.ts's local :(top,literal)

per.section: The fix lands at the mechanism

acceptance: No src/ or harness/ git invocation matches a host-composed path as a pattern; one spelling, three call surfaces adopting it.
tests: job rm on a glob-metacharacter job name leaves a sibling job's files tracked
job new on a glob-metacharacter job name leaves a dirty sibling job unstaged
commitPaths stages only its given path when a sibling name glob-matches it
pins: a window diff narrows by a path whose name carries a glob metacharacter
notes: Measured git 2.43. Over-match, not under-match: exact-literal always matches, so a metachar name matches itself AND its glob siblings — `git add -- '.flume/jobs/a*'` stages sibling `ab` too. Three spellings exist today: `--literal-pathspecs` (main-command position only, ls-tree exits 129 on it), `GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1` (any position), `:(top,literal)` prefix (anchors at repo root). validateJobName admits `*`/`[`; job rm's `git rm -r` over the glob is the destructive end.
